intent: Refine sensor positions by moving the front-center sensor slightly forward to y=0.065 m to enhance forward line sensing, while keeping sensor size at 0.016 m and wheel track at 0.14 m for stability. Expect sustained zero line loss, improved anticipation of line curvature, and potentially smoother steering with low oscillation and error.
rationale: The previous iteration's geometry with larger sensors (0.016 m), an added front-center sensor at y=0.06 m, and a wider wheel track (0.14 m) showed excellent performance on both the oval and s-bend tracks, with zero line loss events and low steering oscillation. The telemetry confirms stable line detection and smooth control, with no line loss and near-complete progress on both tracks. Given this strong performance, I maintain the sensor size at 0.016 m and the wheel track at 0.14 m to preserve stability and line detection quality. I propose a slight refinement in sensor positions to optimize forward sensing and lateral coverage: reposition the front-center sensor slightly forward to y=0.065 m to better anticipate line curvature, and adjust lateral sensors to maintain balanced coverage. The body dimensions, wheel radius, and mass remain unchanged to keep the robot's dynamics consistent. This geometry aims to sustain the high completion rate and low error observed, potentially improving control smoothness further. I request measurements including steering_oscillation, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, completion, and progress to verify stability and line following robustness on all tracks.
